A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TREECUT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six LLMs, controlled experiments on problem structure, and manual analysis of hallucinated answers.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds few-shot results, alongside revised unanswerable-problem results.

M1.justification: The tree construction, equation generation, edge-cutting procedure, and Algorithms 1-2 are unchanged. The added verbalization templates document an existing component; few-shot prompting is an evaluation condition, not a revision to TREECUT.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic answerable and unanswerable arithmetic word problems with the same depth, tree-complexity, naming, and cut-location scenarios. Larger samples and few-shot prompting do not introduce new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain Llama 3.1 Instruct 8B/70B, Qwen2.5 Instruct 7B/72B, GPT-4o, and o3-mini. The new few-shot comparison uses this same set.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 increase the reported problem count from 100 to 500 per configuration; the answerable evaluation explicitly remains at 100. Section 4.2 adds a substantially different prompting protocol using three answerable and three unanswerable worked examples. These establish reported protocol changes without proving that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The new few-shot comparison across all six models and four depths substantially extends the analysis to whether hallucinations persist after demonstrations of correct abstention. The existing structural sensitivity experiments and Appendix C cases, including the 20-response manual audit, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Increasing the number of generated problems changes sample size, not uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the earlier estimates under larger reported samples: GPT-4o at depth 8 changes from 61% to 64%, and o3-mini at depth 2 from 42% to 44%. New Table 2 adds few-shot results, including o3-mini rates of 2.4%-3.6%. Figures 2-3 update plotted values while retaining broad trends. The answerable results are unchanged, moving from Table 2 to Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical constraints and reasoning connecting tree paths, calculability, and missing conditions are unchanged. The new formula-translation cases explain how existing equations become sentences; they add no substantive mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions and qualitative claims about controllable problem generation and structural triggers of hallucination remain the same. The abstract updates numerical rates and explicitly names the zero-shot setting already used in v1; the introduction repeats previously stated findings.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets o3-mini's few-shot improvement as suppression of unsupported assumptions and persistent failures of the other models as intrinsic recognition difficulties. The limitations statement now covers zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Existing domain limitations and Appendix C explanations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 reports available generation code and sample data with an access location. Appendix A adds explicit verbalization templates, and Appendix B.2 identifies gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and o3-mini-2025-01-31. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed model versions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Patel et al. (2021), Kumar et al. (2021), Xu et al. (2022), and Liu et al. (2021), expanding robustness and tree-based augmentation context. The central positioning relative to MathGAP and existing unanswerable benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work receive localized expansions and rewriting. v2 adds explanatory passages and acknowledgements and makes Limitations unnumbered, while retaining the overall section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the few-shot table and a boxed formula-translation template. The answerable table becomes Table 3, Figure 3 moves to the following page, and appendix material reflows. The overall layout, figure designs, and table formats remain similar.

improvement.justification: The few-shot control addresses v1's acknowledged prompting limitation and provides useful evidence of o3-mini's prompt dependence. Templates, model identifiers, and reported code access also improve reproducibility. Integration remains incomplete: Section 4.4 retains 61%/42% despite the abstract and Table 1 reporting 64%/44%, and Section 4.2 overgeneralizes the other models' mixed few-shot changes as largely unchanged. The net improvement is useful but limited.
